subject: Camera traps: false-positives and gregarious species

messages.author: a655eab1a44752d2
messages.subject: Camera traps: false-positives and gregarious species
parts:
Dear all,

I have count data from camera traps (210 sites, 25 occasions at each), and would like some advice on approaches to model abundance of solitary (e.g. Agouti) and gregarious (e.g. White-lipped Peccary) unmarked species, for whom is it not possible to diferentiate individuals at the same site and occasion.
Since camera trap effective sampled area is around 20 m x 6 m plot (the area in front of camera at which sensor can detect some animal), and it is a small area considering species' home ranges and daily movements,
to adopt a Temporary Emigration N-mix model (Chandler at al., Ecology 92(7) 2011, gpcount in unmarked) sounds important.

In Marc and Royle's AHME book, they suggest the use of N-mix Poisson/Poisson for solitary species with probable many false-positives
on counts at the same site and occasion (the same individual recorded many times). Should the use of a Poisson distribution for counts in a model aslo considering Temporary Emigration (instead of a Binomial, as in gpcount) be the best option for these species?

For gregarious species, AHME book suggest the choice of a beta-binomial underlying the count in N-mix model. To apply a beta-bionmial in a Temp Emig N-mix model would be the best option?
For each independent group record we have the minimum number of different individuals of the group, and maybe group size could be modeled considering spatial covariates. Is there such approach for N-mix models?

Thanks for any comment!

Cheers,

Igor
